prose:
The readable opening of JA Westenberg's paid essay argues that people, law and habit will shape the pace at which AI is absorbed into society, reversing the familiar software-eating-the-world metaphor. It signals an institutional and cultural argument rather than a simple technical adoption curve.

The article body was paywalled, so its cases, evidence, detailed claims and conclusion were not read. The headline and subtitle cannot support reconstructing an entire argument, a numerical adoption forecast or a claim that the author rejects all AI uses. No subscription or access bypass was attempted.
highlights: Coverage is limited to title, subtitle and opening
Essay emphasizes social and institutional friction
Full examples and conclusions remain unread
No numerical adoption estimate is established
No comprehensive view is inferred from the title
No paywall bypass or subscription was attempted
